gaz_identification: Sehwan (Lambrick's candidate for 臂多勢羅; alternative only)
local_evidence: At the Arab conquest (711) the governors of the forts were generally Buddhists, and the principal citizens of Sehwan were Buddhists who would not fight for Dahar.
quote: the principal citizens were Buddhists and would not fight for him
note: No Xuanzang link. Buddhists at Sehwan c. 711 fit Xuanzang's 臂多勢羅 (50 monasteries, 3000 Sammatīya monks), but equally the other Sindh countries.

gaz_identification: Las Bela (Mirchandani's 阿點婆翅羅; alternative only)
local_evidence: Index: Chach succeeds Sahasi II in 631 and subdues Las Bela.
quote: succeeded by Ohack (A D 631) who subdues Las Beyla
note: Supports Mirchandani's point that Las Bela was subject to Sind from c. 631, as Xuanzang says of 阿點婆翅羅 (統屬信度國); the same holds for the delta.
Kalian Kot (near Tatta) with large "Buddhist" bricks, compared with Kafir Killa near Sehwan; no Xiyu ji place.

gaz_identification: Vijnot (Banfill's candidate for 毘苫婆補羅, cited by Mirchandani; alternative only)
local_evidence: Old Hindu city of Vijnot, 4 miles S of Reti station: carved slabs and brick foundations.
quote: In the old Hindu city of Vijnot, 4 miles south of Reti railway station, are found carved slabs, brick foundations
note: No Xuanzang link in the gazetteer.

gaz_identification: Kaikanan, an Arab district possibly including Dera Ghazi Khan
local_evidence: Ibn Haukal mentions Arab principalities W of Mansura and Multan; one, possibly Kaikanan, "not identified", probably included Dera Ghazi Khan.
quote: possibly Kaikanan, a district frequently mentioned by the Arab chroniclers, but not identified
note: The Arab Kaikanan is Mirchandani's equation for 稽疆那 (he puts it in Quetta–Pishin); this gazetteer puts it near Dera Ghazi Khan. Neither cites Xuanzang here.

gaz_identification: Alor (the study's capital for 毘苫婆補羅)
local_evidence: Ruins of Aror on hilly ground over the old river bed: very large "Hindu" bricks, coins after rain, a mosque attributed to Aurangzeb.
quote: Hindu bricks of the very large kind are found and after rain coins have been unearthed
note: Site evidence for the Alor capital; no Xuanzang link in this passage.
